notes.text: Kailer Yamamoto is day to day (upper body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Michael Carcone has taken his spot beside Anders Lee and Barrett Hayton.

John Marino is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Andrew Peeke has taken his spot beside Nate Schmidt. That pair has had 55% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 72:38 together, about what it had with Marino (59%).

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 27% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Warren Foegele is out 3-4 weeks and has missed the last 2 games.
William Eklund is out 10-12 weeks and has missed the last 11 games.
Jonas Johansson was added to the roster on Oct 23.
Jordan Spence has started killing penalties: on the ice for 25% of the team’s shorthanded time in 15 games, up from 4% last season.

stakes: The Mammoth go in second in the Central with 18 points, the Senators third in the Atlantic with 19 points.

story.head: Iron sharpens iron
paras: The Mammoth (9-6-0) lost 6-3 to Philadelphia on Sunday, while the Senators (9-5-1) beat San Jose 5-1 on Oct 31. Going in, the Mammoth are second in the Central (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Senators third in the Atlantic (tied for sixth).

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.600) says: their chances are worth about .729, and their goaltending has held them back. The Senators’ record (.633) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.563), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

The Mammoth (1st) and the Senators (2nd) both rarely get pinned in their own end. The Mammoth roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd). As for the Senators, they play slow, tight games (3rd lowest) and draw more penalties than they take (4th). The Mammoth’s good looks will be harder to come by against the Sens. On top of that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Clayton Keller (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 15 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring. Logan Cooley (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high eight goals, with eight points in his last five games. Tim Stützle (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 15 GP) leads the Senators in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Drake Batherson (9 G / 8 A / 17 P in 15 GP) is next in line, with ten points in his last five games.
Karel Vejmelka (6-5-0 / .868 SV% in 11 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Utah, but will likely start. Jonas Johansson (1-1-0 / .859 SV% in 3 GS) is in line to start for Ottawa.
At home, Travis Green likes to send Amadio, Giroux and Greig out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Keller, Schmaltz and Guenther.

The Mammoth are newly without Kailer Yamamoto, and have been without John Marino since Oct 17.
Ridly Greig has scored in four straight games against Utah.
Tim Stützle has nine goals on chances worth about 4.8 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
